title: RollbackReport
description: What a rollback to a log coordinate did ({§log-wire-format}): the file mutations it reversed, latest first, each as an ordinary operation of the acting client; the rows it could not reverse because they kept no patch; and, when it stopped, the row and path where the file no longer matched what that mutation wrote.

to.description: The coordinate rolled back to, `<loop>/<turn>/<item>`; the state after that item is what remains.

action.description: What the reversal did to the file: rewrote it, recreated a removed file, or removed a created one.

reason.description: no-patch: the row kept no patch (a byte write, a member past the materialization bound, or a row settled before patches were kept). already-reversed: the file is in the state before that mutation, so an earlier rollback reversed it; nothing is done again.
drift: the file no longer holds what that mutation wrote, so nothing was restored for it or for anything earlier; refused: the reversing operation was refused, and its Problem is the detail.
